latestPosts.caption:
"Always have a man on the call with you." 

Investors told her that.
She was the founder.
She was the CEO.

I asked Beth Flippo, founder and CEO of Dexa, if being a woman impacted her fundraising.

Her answer: investors would finish a call with her and ask which man on her team they should talk to about the technical stuff. 

Her own male executives watched it happen.
Only then did they believe it was real.

Only 1.8% of funding goes to women.
The bias is not really debatable.

But the founders who get the least funding are building stronger revenue companies.
Nothing was handed to them.

Full Episode link in bio

Comment SEEN if this has happened to you.
#WomenFounders #Fundraising #WomenInTech #TenacityPodca

latestPosts.caption:
Before revenue, there is belief.
And the founder has to sell it.

Beth Flippo had to stop flying her drones just to save money while she raised.
She had never raised before.
She was not in Silicon Valley.
And only 1.8% of funding goes to women.

My take: it is easier to sell with an MVP or revenue.
Most founders start with neither.

So what carries you?
Belief, sold honestly, until the results catch up.

Full Episode link on Bio
Comment BELIEF if you have had to sell the vision before the proof.

#Fundraising #StartupLife #WomenFounders #TenacityPodcast

latestPosts.caption:
Everyone has an idea. Very few build a company from it.
Beth Flippo, founder and CEO of Dexa, told me the difference.
Her rule is simple.
An investor or a customer has to want it.

Or do not start.

She chose one target, Kroger, because within 3 miles of a store, you reach 100 million people. Then she put 100% of her energy there.

Founders, are you building, or are you still just holding an idea?

Full Episode link in bio
Comment IDEA if you are building something real.

latestPosts.caption:
Getting a job doesn’t automatically mean someone has everything they need to succeed.

For many women facing barriers to employment, the challenge isn’t just finding an opportunity. It’s having the mental health support, stability, and resources to move forward.

We often talk about helping women get back into the workforce. But what happens when we overlook everything they’re carrying outside of work?

In this conversation on Tenacity with Sonia C., we explore why mental health support matters and why creating real opportunities means looking at the whole person, not just their résumé.

Because getting hired is one step. Having the support to stay, grow, and thrive is another.

Here’s a question for employers and business leaders: Are we creating workplaces where women can truly succeed, or are we just focused on getting them through the door?

🎙️ Watch the conversation and share your thoughts below.

#supportingwoman #MentalHealthMatters #WomenEmpowerment #InclusiveHiring

latestPosts.caption:
Founders track revenue. Profit. Growth. Customer acquisition.

But what about joy?

In my conversation with Bianca B. King, she shared something that stuck with me.

One of her biggest warning signs of burnout isn't how many hours she's working.

It's whether she's still enjoying the work.

And I think there's something important here.

You can work hard, build a successful business, and still recognize when something isn't right.

Joy isn't a replacement for revenue or profit. But losing it completely might be telling you something about how you're running your business.

Founders, when was the last time you actually enjoyed running your company?

#TenacityWithSoniaC #FounderBurnout #Entrepreneurship #FounderLife
latestPosts.alt: Video by Tenacity with Sonia C on October 29, 2026. May be a graphic of one or more people, magazine, poster and text.

latestPosts.caption:
Sometimes the ambition that gets you through the hardest parts of your life becomes the very thing that burns you out.

Bianca left home at 13. Slept on her sister's sofa for two years. Put herself through school. Then went on to work on over $1.4 billion in real estate deals.

On paper, she was successful.

But by 32, she was burned out.

She calls it toxic ambition.

And it raises a question I think more founders need to ask themselves:

Are you still building your business like you're trying to survive?

#FounderBurnout #ToxicAmbition #Entrepreneurship #TenacityWithSoniaC
